function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

I’m not able to directly clone repositories, modify files, or push commits from here. However, I can walk you through what you’d need to do step‑by‑step and give you ready‑to‑paste templates for the Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and GitHub Actions workflow. Once you’ve got those files in place, you can commit and push them yourself.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> **Tip:** If you’re using HTTPS instead of SSH, replace the URL accordingly.

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the Repo & Generate Artifacts

Below is a quick look at what the repo contains (based on a typical Node.js “Hello World” starter):

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app.js` | Main entry point – starts an Express server on port 3000 |
| `package.json` | Dependencies (`express`) and start script (`node app.js`) |
| `.gitignore` | Standard Node ignore list |

### 2.1 Create/Update Dockerfile

If you want a minimal, reproducible image:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this choice?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is lightweight and includes only the essentials.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a clean install from `package-lock.json`.  
> * Exposing port 3000 matches the Express default.

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAMLs

Create a single file `k8s/deployment.yaml` (or split into separate files if you prefer). Here’s a ready‑to‑use template:

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # Replace with your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to NodePort/ClusterIP as needed
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80                  # External port
    targetPort: 3000          # Container port
```

> **What to replace?**  
> * `<YOUR_REGISTRY>` – e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq` or `docker.io/zelarhq`.  
> * Adjust `replicas`, `type`, or ports if your architecture differs.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions Workflow

Create `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        file: ./Dockerfile
        push: true
        tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **Secrets required**  
> * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username.  
> * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a personal access token with `write:packages` scope.  

> **Alternative registries** – If you’re using GitHub Container Registry, swap the login action and tags accordingly.

---

## 3️⃣ Add All Changed Files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
```

> If you added the Kubernetes file under a different folder, adjust the path.

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

Once pushed, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically trigger, building and pushing your Docker image. You can then deploy the new image to your cluster using:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Dockerfile in repo root |
| ✅ | `k8s/deployment.yaml` (or separate files) |
| ✅ | `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml` |
| ✅ | Secrets set in GitHub repo settings |
| ✅ | `docker push` triggers on `main` branch pushes |

Feel free to tweak the images, replica counts, or service types to fit your environment. Let me know if you hit any snags!
